review_notes: I read the whole file and the dependency `sq_eq_one_of_smul_one_mem_orthogonalGroup`. I also read the downstream use in AlgebraicGroup/SpecialOrthogonal/Center.lean. I did not look up the Mathlib lemma names the replacement proof would need (Matrix.det_unique, Fintype.card_eq_one_iff and similar), so that proof sketch is untested. Other statements looked appropriately general: the ring is an arbitrary commutative ring, the index type is arbitrary, and the scalar/center characterisation needs both dimension ≥ 3 and regularity of 2. `IsRegular (2:R)` could be weakened to `IsLeftRegular`, because only `h2.left` is used and the ring is commutative. I judged that too marginal to report.

findings.problem: The hypothesis `3 ≤ Fintype.card n` is only a side condition for `mem_center_iff`. Odd dimension already gives `1 ≤ Fintype.card n`. The only case the bound excludes is dimension 1, where `specialOrthogonalGroup n R` is trivial because `det g = g default default = 1`. So the odd-dimension triviality is true without `hn`, but the statement is restricted to n ≥ 3 and the docstring repeats the restriction. The intended mathematics is not changed; the statement is just narrower than the truth.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma as `theorem eq_one_of_mem_center_of_odd (h2 : IsRegular (2 : R)) (g : specialOrthogonalGroup n R) (hodd : Odd (Fintype.card n)) (hg : g ∈ Subgroup.center (specialOrthogonalGroup n R)) : g = 1`. For the proof, do `by_cases hn : 3 ≤ Fintype.card n`. If it holds, run the current argument unchanged. Otherwise `Odd (card n)` forces `Fintype.card n = 1`, since card 0 is even and card 2 is even. Then `Fintype.card_eq_one_iff` gives a `Unique n`. `Matrix.det_unique` together with `(mem_specialOrthogonalGroup_iff.mp g.2).2` shows the single entry is 1, and `Subtype.ext` plus `ext i j` (with i = j = default) closes the goal. Equivalently, the 1×1 case could be a separate lemma.
findings.benefit: Callers no longer have to prove an artificial `3 ≤ n` for odd n. The downstream `eq_one_of_isCentralPoint_of_odd` needs `hn` only for `isCentralPoint_iff_mem_center_pointsMulEquiv`, so it also becomes easier to generalise. The result becomes the clean statement that every odd-dimensional special orthogonal group has trivial center, with n = 1 covered.
